1 فَضَا , (M, Msb, K,) aor. يَفْضُو, (M, Msb,) inf. n. فُضُوٌّ (M, Msb, K) and فَضَآءٌ, (M, K,) It (a place) was, or became, wide, or spacious; (M, Msb, K;) as also ↓ افضى ; (TA as from the K, in which I do not find it;) the latter occurring in a trad., and expl. in the Nh as signifying it became a فَضَآء [q. v.]. (TA.) ―
-b2- [And It was, or became, empty, vacant, or void; (for it is said in the TA that الفضو, by which الفُضُوُّ is evidently meant, signifies الخُلُوُّ;) as also ↓ افضى , as appears from an explanation of the part. n. مُفْضٍ, q. v.] ―
-b3- فَضَا الشَّجَرُ بِالمَكَانِ, inf. n. فضو [i. e. فُضُوٌّ], The trees became numerous, or abundant, [so as to occupy much space,] in the place. (IKtt, TA.) ―
-b4- And فَضَا دَرَاهِمَهُ He did not put his dirhems, or money, into the purse [app. meaning that he left his money strewn]. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
